statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH (yellow). Tail is in the watch band because two days of unpriced weekend news - an AI-pacing call from the Anthropic and OpenAI chief executives that is expected to weigh on semiconductors, and a fatal vessel strike in the Strait of Hormuz - reach a halted market that reopens at 22:00 UTC into the thinnest liquidity of the week, while Stress stays high on a pre-FOMC rates and energy backdrop with the 10-year near 5%.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the mapped state is WATCH for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. One narrow window is flagged: 22:00-02:00 UTC spanning the Globex reopen, where the unpriced AI-pacing and Gulf headlines meet the thinnest liquidity of the week. A secondary checkpoint sits at the 13:30 UTC US cash open on Monday, where the forecast re-enters the watch band.
headline: Nasdaq-100 reopens at 22:00 UTC carrying an unpriced AI-pacing debate and a fatal Hormuz strike, into a hawkish Fed week with the 10-year near 5%
body: CME equity futures are shut until 22:00 UTC, so no live NQ price path exists at assessment time. The last observed tape is Friday's: the Nasdaq-100 closed at 29,368.44, up 0.91%, inside a 29,313.51-29,473.12 range and roughly 105 points below the session high, so the index was not pinned at an extreme, while VIX fell 11.21% to 15.84. That structure is orderly and retracement-friendly, which keeps Tail below the blocking threshold. The backdrop is tighter than the tape suggests. The latest H.15 release shows the 10-year at 4.95%, the 2-year at 4.56% and the 30-year at 5.37%, with reporting noting the 2-year touched 4.596% on Friday, its highest since July 2024, as a global bond selloff pushed the 10-year toward 5% on oil and rate-hike fears. WTI settled near $100 and Brent near $104.61 after Friday pullbacks of 2.4% and 2.8%, but both still gained roughly 9-10% on the week. CME FedWatch put the probability of a quarter-point hike at Wednesday's FOMC at 85.6% on Friday, up from 48.4% a month earlier, with the press conference half an hour after the decision. Equities near record highs with VIX under 16 against that stack is a thin cushion, which is why Stress is high while Tail is not. Two unpriced weekend stacks sit between this assessment and the reopen. The first is Nasdaq-specific: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published an essay on Saturday arguing for pacing the rate of AI capability advancement, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman backed the proposal and Elon Musk agreed, and reporting expects semiconductors to bear the brunt of any initial repricing. Commentary is genuinely two-sided: one prominent investor called for AI stocks to drop 10%+, while others argue the multi-year spending trajectory is unchanged, and the US president said on Sunday that 'very negative forces' are raising exaggerated concerns over AI. The second stack is the Gulf: an Iranian commercial vessel was struck near Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz late Saturday, killing one and wounding four, while Iran and GCC foreign ministers are due to meet in Salalah on Monday on a new maritime route through the strait, with Bahrain having said it will not attend. That checkpoint is two-sided, since a shipping arrangement would ease the energy impulse that has been driving yields. Neither stack has produced observed one-way price structure, so the mapped policy state is caution rather than a block, concentrated in the reopen window.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding published hours were available and uniformly green with the mapped state EA_ON. Tail held flat at 6 from late Saturday through the overnight hours, then drifted up from 05:00 UTC to 17 by 15:00 UTC as the weekend ran toward the futures reopen, easing to 16 and then stepping to 17, 18, 18 and 19 across the final five hours. Stress rose steadily from 53 to 76 as the pre-FOMC rates and energy backdrop accumulated, the dominant mode stayed normal throughout, and Confidence held near 86 before stepping down to the low 70s from 16:00 UTC as the weekend evidence gap widened.
outlookSummary: The window splits into three phases. Until 22:00 UTC the CME equity complex is closed and no price path can form, so the current watch-band reading is a forward allowance rather than a reading of observed structure. The 22:00-02:00 UTC stretch spanning the Globex reopen is the concentrated conditional risk point, where two unpriced stacks - the Anthropic and OpenAI pacing call with semiconductors most exposed, and the Hormuz vessel strike - can reprice into the thinnest liquidity of the week; Tail peaks at 24 there as a gap allowance, not as an observed move, and the specific invalidation to watch is repeated extension with shallow or failed pullbacks. From the Asian hours onward the base case is absorption of any gap and a return to two-way trade, with Tail decaying toward 16 through the European session. A secondary conditional checkpoint follows at the 13:30 UTC US cash open, where any AI-sector repricing meets its deepest liquidity for the first time and the forecast re-enters the watch band for two hours before decaying again. Monday's US calendar holds only routine bill auctions at 15:30 UTC, so residual risk is headline-driven, with crude the main transmission channel and the Salalah Iran-GCC meeting an unresolved two-sided checkpoint. Stress stays in the high band throughout because the underlying tension - a hike priced at 85.6%, a 10-year near 5%, crude near $100 and two open headline stacks - does not resolve before Wednesday's FOMC.
